--- a/prompt.md
+++ b/prompt.md
@@ -8,6 +8,8 @@
 - Compute the answer in Python and write the resulting LITERAL value into each answer cell. Do NOT leave an Excel formula (a string beginning with `=`, such as `=IF(...)`, `=SUMIFS(...)`, `=XLOOKUP(...)`) as a cell's value: grading reads the stored value, and a formula that uses an unsupported or volatile function (XLOOKUP, TODAY, NOW, …) or that is not recalculated is then compared as raw formula text and scores zero. Even when the instruction asks for a formula, work out what that formula would evaluate to and store the resulting value(s). (Applying conditional-formatting rules or cell formatting is different — do that as formatting, not as a cell value.)
 - Your exact solution code is automatically re-run on two more input files that share the same layout but hold DIFFERENT data (different rows, dates, counts, and values), and every run is graded. Write GENERAL code that derives every value, row/column count, boundary, cutoff, threshold, and index from the file it opens at run time (e.g. from `ws.max_row` or the actual data extent, not a fixed number). Do not hardcode a number, date, label, cell address, or count that you read from the preview or observed while inspecting the sample file — a solution that pastes answers computed for the sample will be wrong on the other two files.
+- If the answer cells, a neighbouring reference cell, or a demonstrated example row/column already hold an actual Excel FORMULA for the computation (e.g. `=$G$8/365*N4`, `=B2-B3`, `=D2-D4`, `=IF(AND(G15<1.05,G15>0.95),"PASS","FAIL")`), treat that formula as the exact specification of the METHOD. Reproduce its precise cell references, its constants (e.g. divide by 365 if it does, and note per-row differences such as one column using `=D2-D4` while another uses `=B2-B3`), its inclusive/exclusive boundaries, its rounding, and the exact output text it produces — do NOT swap in a different method that merely looks equivalent (e.g. do not replace an explicit `/365` with a per-row day count, and do not replace the literal per-cell references with a generic "nth-largest value" heuristic) — then apply any additional step the instruction adds. Reading a constant or cell reference that the sheet's OWN formula defines is reading the specification, not the forbidden hardcoding above, because you re-read the referenced cells at run time so it still adapts to the other two files.
+- A pre-filled SAMPLE ANSWER is NOT such a specification: an "Expected Result"/example-output column, or worked answer cells that show what the sample file should produce, holds only the sample's answers. Never copy those displayed values into your output — the other two graded files hold different data, so the sample's answers will be wrong there. Compute every answer yourself with the general method above (and read the referenced source cells, not the example-answer cells, at run time).
 - Always save your result to the exact output_path given, creating any missing parent directories first.
 - If code execution returns an error, read the traceback carefully and fix the code — do not repeat a failing approach unchanged.
 
-Before treating the task as finished, verify your final code: (1) writes computed data values — not VBA/macro source, an explanation, or an Excel formula string — into answer_position; (2) derives all values, ranges, and boundaries from the input file rather than hardcoding constants observed in the sample; and (3) modifies only answer_position and saves to the exact output_path.
+Before treating the task as finished, verify your final code: (1) writes computed data values — not VBA/macro source, an explanation, or an Excel formula string — into answer_position; (2) derives all values, ranges, and boundaries from the input file rather than hardcoding constants observed in the sample; (3) modifies only answer_position and saves to the exact output_path; and (4) where the sheet already supplies a formula for the computation, reproduces THAT exact formula's method (its references, constants, boundaries, and output text) rather than a look-alike, while never copying pre-filled sample or "Expected Result" answer values.
